title: Change your settings
summary: How to change the business details, GST basis and BAS frequency, your bank accounts, and how the app looks.

sections.heading: What Settings shows
paragraphs: Settings is a set of cards. Each says in one line whether all is well. Anything that needs attention is listed at the top, and its card comes first.

image.description: The Settings page with its cards: Backups, Google, Business, Bank accounts, Admin Dashboard, Appearance and About.

steps.text: In the Business card, click Change…
Change the business name or ABN. The ABN is checked, so a typing mistake is caught.

Choose Cash or Accrual for GST, and Quarterly or Monthly for the BAS. Check with your accountant first: reports and the BAS worksheet for periods not yet locked are then worked out the new way. Locked periods do not change.

image.description: The Business sheet: business name, ABN, GST basis Cash or Accrual, BAS frequency Quarterly or Monthly with Monthly chosen, the fixed financial year 1 July to 30 June, and a warning that open periods will be worked out the new way.

steps.text: Click Save. The financial year always runs 1 July to 30 June.
Before you import a statement file for an account, add it here. Click Add bank account…
Type a name, the bank, and the last four digits of the account number. Only those four digits are kept, and a statement file is matched to its account by them.
Choose the account in your chart that holds its balance, such as Business cheque account, and click Add.
Rename changes the name. Stop using keeps its transactions but stops new files for it from importing; it asks first.
In the Appearance card, choose Same as Mac, Light or Dark. The app changes at once.

sections.heading: If something goes wrong
paragraphs: A statement file says the account is not one of your bank accounts: add it in Bank accounts, with the same last four digits.
The ABN is refused: check its 11 digits against your ABN registration.
